info.title: openmediavault-webui contract
info.description: The backend methods the openmediavault web interface calls, described from OMV's source and from replies captured on a test system. Nothing on the server reads this document.

post.description: Sign in with a user name and password. Wrong credentials are HTTP 400; too many failed second-factor attempts for the user are HTTP 429. Never retried automatically (UI-14).

429.description: Too many failed second-factor attempts for this user. The reply says no wait time (A10).

post.description: Answer the pending challenge of Session.login. HTTP 400 for a wrong code; 429 from the third failure on, with a growing delay; 401 when no login is pending or it expired (A10).

401.description: No login is pending, or it expired (300 s) or was discarded by another call.

429.description: Too many wrong codes. The delay grows from 5 s to 300 s; the reply does not say how long (A10).

post.description: End the session. Returns null.
Host, version, load and memory, and whether configuration changes are pending. A user gets only the time and host name.

401.description: No session, or it ended. The first call after the idle timeout says so; later ones say there is no session (A3).

post.description: True when saved settings have not been applied yet.
Deploy the pending configuration changes, as a background task. Services may restart. The task's result is the list of modules deployed.
Throw away every saved change that has not been applied, as a background task. Nothing is deployed.
Used only by the task helper. Not read-only: the last poll of a finished task deletes it on the server (A6).

500.description: The task failed: the message is the task's whole output (for an apply, the Salt log). Also the answer for a handle the server has already deleted (A6).

post.description: Used only by the task helper, and not for polling: on a finished task it deletes the task, so a later getOutput fails.
Used only by the task helper. Ends the task; the handle is gone afterwards. Returns null.
The SSH service settings.
Save the SSH settings. Nothing changes on the system until the pending changes are applied. Returns the stored settings.
A page of shared folders, sorted and searched by the backend.
The signed-in user's own account.
How long the server keeps an idle session before ending it. Every signed-in user can read it.
The web interface's ports, whether it is served over HTTPS, and the session timeout.

Stop showing the first-sign-in welcome to every administrator, in every browser (`displayWelcomeMessage` in System.getInformation becomes false). Takes effect at once; nothing is left pending. Calling it again when the welcome is already dismissed also succeeds. No method shows the welcome again. Returns null.

Save the signed-in user's own e-mail address and description. The server refuses it (HTTP 500) for a system account such as `admin`, and for an account the administrator does not let its user change (`_readonly` in UserMgmt.getUserByContext). The account changes at once; the mail settings (and the SSH settings, when the account has SSH keys) are left pending. Returns the stored account.

200.description: The method's response value, without the fields in x-omv-omit.

500.description: The account may not be changed by its user.

post.description: Change the signed-in user's own password. It takes effect at once. The backend does not check `_readonly` here; the interface does. For an account OMV manages (not a system account such as `admin`), the server also leaves the mail settings, and the SSH settings when the account has SSH keys, pending (observed on OMV 8.6.1). Returns null.
The system's host name and domain name.
The time zone, whether the clock is set from time servers, and the server's current date.

How the system sends notification e-mail. The server's reply also carries the SMTP password in plain text; the transport removes it before the reply is validated, cached or returned (UI-6), so no page can show or keep it.

200.description: The method's response value, without the fields in x-omv-omit.

ConfigAppliedModules.description: The result of an apply task (its final output, parsed as JSON) - the modules deployed.

Username.description: An account name, in OMV's `username` format.

Role.description: The session's role. `admin` is an administrator; anything else is treated as a user.

SessionAuthenticated.description: A signed-in session. The server also sends `sessionid`; the transport ignores it and it is not described here (UI-6). The session lives in OMV's HttpOnly cookie.

SessionChallengeRequired.description: The password was right and a second factor is required. The interface shows its own screen for each `kind` it knows (A10). The server also sends `challenge.redirecturl`, a route of the stock interface; it is ignored and not described here (UI-3). No other call may be made before Session.verify: any call discards the pending challenge.

kind.description: The second-factor method, e.g. `totp`. An unknown kind sends the user to the classic interface.

RpcErrorDetail.description: The `error` member of an rpc.php failure reply. The transport turns it into an RpcError with the HTTP status; its `trace` is discarded at once and never described here (UI-9). `code` is 0 for every error observed (A8), so the status and the message are the only signals.

message.description: The backend's message, already translated by the server. Shown as text.

SessionVerifyRequest.description: The answer to a `totp` challenge (openmediavault-2fa-totp, A10). OMV's core accepts any value here and hands it to the two-factor plugin; the contract accepts only the one shape the interface sends.

SystemInformation.description: System information. Every signed-in user gets `ts`, `time` and `hostname`; an administrator also gets the rest.

ts.description: Unix time on the server, in seconds.

time.description: Display text, the server's local time in the server's locale.

memUtilization.description: A fraction from 0 to 1, as a decimal string (A4).

dirtyModules.description: Module name to the module's description (display text). An empty map arrives as `[]`; the transport turns it into `{}`.

modules.description: Ask about these modules only. Empty or absent asks about every module.
The modules to deploy. Empty deploys every dirty module.

force.description: Deploy the listed modules even if they are not dirty; with no modules, every module.

TaskHandle.description: A background task handle: the server path of the task's status file. Opaque. Held in memory only, never shown, never put in a URL or storage, and passed to Exec only by the task helper (UI-5).

filename.description: Always empty, as the stock interface sends; the server finds the revision itself.

pos.description: Byte offset to read from; the `pos` of the previous reply.

ExecOutput.description: New output of a task since `pos`. The poll that reports `running: false` with nothing pending is the last one: the server then deletes the task, and any further call on the handle fails (A6). A failed task makes this call itself fail, with the task's output as the message.

output.description: Plain text since the requested position, line endings normalised to newlines.

extraoptions.description: Extra lines for the SSH server's configuration file. Free text.

GetListRequest.description: Paging, sorting and search for a list (rpc.common.getlist). The backend sorts and searches the whole list. `limit` null returns every row (A2). OMV also accepts an integer `search`; the contract accepts text only.

perms.description: 0 no access, 5 read-only, 7 read and write.

SharedFolder.description: A shared folder (conf.system.sharedfolder) with the fields ShareMgmt computes.

mntentref.description: The UUID of the file system's mount point.

reldirpath.description: The folder's path inside its file system.

privileges.description: The privileges set on the folder; the empty string when none are set (observed).

_used.description: True if another configuration object refers to this folder.

device.description: The file system's label, else its device file; empty if unknown.

description.description: Display text built by the server.

status.description: OK, or why the folder cannot be reached.

items.description: A public key in RFC 4716 format.

_readonly.description: True if the administrator does not let this user change their account.

AutoLogoutSettings.description: The session timeout, from the web administration settings (conf.webadmin). The server ends a session that has been idle this long.

timeout.description: Minutes. 0 means the server never ends an idle session.

enablessl.description: Whether the web interface is also served over HTTPS.

forcesslonly.description: Whether HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

sslcertificateref.description: The UUID of the certificate used for HTTPS, or empty when none is chosen.

timeout.description: Minutes an idle session lasts. 0 means the server never ends an idle session.

Email.description: An e-mail address, in OMV's `email` format. OMV checks it with PHP's FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL; this pattern accepts a subset of that: a dot-atom local part of at most 64 characters, and a domain of two or more labels whose last starts with a letter. Quoted local parts and address literals, which PHP also accepts, are refused.

UserMgmtSetUserByContextRequest.description: The signed-in user's own e-mail address and description (rpc.usermgmt.setuserbycontext). OMV also accepts `password` here; the contract leaves it out, because the interface changes a password only through UserMgmt.setPasswordByContext.

comment.description: The account's description. The system's account tools refuse a colon or a line break, so the contract does too.

UserByContextSaved.description: The account as UserMgmt.setUserByContext stored it. The server also echoes the password that was submitted (always empty, since the contract does not send one); the contract leaves it out and the transport removes it from the reply (`x-omv-omit`).

disallowusermod.description: True if the administrator does not let this user change their account.

items.description: A public key in RFC 4716 format.

UserMgmtSetPasswordByContextRequest.description: The signed-in user's new password (rpc.usermgmt.setpasswordbycontext). OMV accepts an empty password; the contract does not.

NetworkGeneralSettings.description: The host name and domain name of the system (conf.system.network.dns).

hostname.description: The host name, without the domain.

domainname.description: The domain name, or empty when none is set.

TimeSettings.description: The system clock and time settings (conf.system.time), with the server's current date added by the method.

date.description: The server's date and time when the method ran.

local.description: Display text, the server's local time in the server's locale.

ISO8601.description: The same moment in ISO 8601, with the server's offset from UTC.

timezone.description: The time zone name, e.g. "Etc/UTC" or "Europe/Berlin".

ntpenable.description: Whether the clock is set from time servers.

ntptimeservers.description: The time servers, as one string as OMV stores it.

ntpclients.description: The networks allowed to use this system as a time server, as OMV stores them.

EmailNotificationSettings.description: How the system sends notification e-mail (conf.system.notification.email). The server also sends the SMTP password in plain text; the contract leaves it out and the transport removes it from the reply before anything else sees it (`x-omv-omit` on EmailNotification.get).

enable.description: Whether notifications are sent by e-mail.

server.description: The SMTP server's name or address, or empty.

tls.description: How the connection to the SMTP server is encrypted.

sender.description: The sender's e-mail address, or empty.

primaryemail.description: The address notifications go to, or empty.

secondaryemail.description: A second address notifications go to, or empty.

authenable.description: Whether the system signs in to the SMTP server.

username.description: The user name for the SMTP server, or empty.
